question: Which statement best describes async functions always return a promise?
options: Awaiting one promise then the next runs them sequentially — each waits for the previous to finish. If the operations are independent, that wastes time. Start them together (or use Promise.all) so they run concurrently and you only wait as long as the slowest one.

`await` suspends the surrounding async function until the awaited promise settles, then resumes with the resolved value. Crucially it does NOT block the main thread — control returns to the event loop, so timers, clicks, and other tasks keep running while the function is paused.

Marking a function `async` changes its return type: whatever you return is automatically wrapped in a resolved promise, and any thrown error becomes a rejected promise. This means you can always call `.then()` on the result or `await` it, even if the body looks fully synchronous.

Because `await` turns a rejected promise into a thrown error, you can use ordinary try/catch/finally around awaited calls. This unifies sync and async error handling into one familiar shape, instead of chaining a separate `.catch()`.
